rows.summary: The Underweight call rests on a flawed 'double-counting' argument that treats the trailing/forward P/E gap as priced-in growth. It is further undermined by wrong PEG and compounding arithmetic, by exit triggers that mislabel the 50- and 200-day SMAs, and by an incoherent stop ($960 above an $850 entry, then $910). The price target is underived, key comp and peer figures are invented, and the analyst sections misread the MACD crossover, the 52-week high and fiscal quarter timing, so the report is not fit for publication without substantial rework.

The Underweight call rests on a −$7.9B TTM free-cash-flow figure that the report's own operating cash flow, capex and quarterly FCF data contradict (they imply roughly +$7.5B). The ruling also adopts a flawed margin argument and invented auto-loan and delinquency data. Together with an underived $10.50 target, a debt-to-equity unit error, mismeasured interest coverage and a sizing figure that does not match the stated trim, the report needs substantial rework before publication.

The digest's headline technicals match the computed facts. However, a bull key point overstates the gain from the 52-week low (32% vs 18.6%), and the ruling's 'most important fact', normalized Q2 EPS of $7.00-7.20, is never derived and does not reconcile with the special-items figures. The trade plan's $328 stop is under half an ATR below price ahead of a binary earnings print, the $345 target has no derivation, and the analyst sections contain many misreads, invented comparables, look-ahead social data and presentation lapses.

The Underweight call rests on load-bearing misreads: a seasonal, total-company revenue decline is relabelled an '86% sequential RSV collapse', a Q1 figure is passed off as Q2 2025 to manufacture a 62% YoY drop, and cash burn is called accelerating when it is narrowing. The $130 target, stop and re-entry zone are a single underived level wrongly justified by the bull and bear models, and the report also carries fabricated peer comparables and clinical figures, stale 52-week and market-cap data, numerous arithmetic slips and presentation defects.

The price-derived figures in the digest match the computed facts, but the headline thesis rests on misread trends. FCF conversion has actually improved for two quarters, operating margin is up YoY, and the stock is not at new highs. The $560 target is underived and contradicts the manager's below-market fair value, while stops, triggers and entry zones conflict across sections and single StockTwits posts are treated as fact.

The price-derived digest figures match the computed facts, but the ruling and portfolio thesis lean on non-GAAP margin, net-retention and cRPO claims that appear nowhere in the inputs. The headline $5.15B FCF does not reconcile with the quarterly data, and key bull/bear points misread periods and margins. The exit trigger, price target and stop are poorly constructed: the margin trigger is already breached, the target is underived, and the stop is sized below one ATR.

The report's price-derived technicals are mostly accurate, but the debate and ruling rest on invented or miscomputed figures. These include an unsupported 11%→33% inventory-ratio surge, a +2% QoQ profit 'red flag' that is an artifact of investment gains, a wrong PEG, wrong scenario-weighted returns, and an underived $265 target. Numerous arithmetic, labeling (YoY vs QoQ, D/E units, fiscal periods) and internal-consistency errors, plus agent-name and emoji leakage, mean it is not fit for publication without substantial rework.

The price-derived technicals in the digest match the computed facts, but load-bearing points rest on misread data: a 74.72% D/E shown as 74.72x, a 'Fed cut' to a rate above current Fed funds, interest coverage placed in a Debt/EBITDA band, and a bear point whose title contradicts its own detail. The Underweight rating is paired with an underived $60 target 11.6% above the price, and key exit triggers rest on unsourced thresholds, so the note is not fit to publish without substantial rework.

The report reaches a defensible Hold, but several load-bearing points are wrong. Debt-to-equity is misread as 65x, gross margin is called a five-quarter high when it slipped, the $75 stop is described as below the $66.60 low, a 17.8% margin is said to exceed 18.7%, the TTM EBITDA and FCF figures behind the headline leverage claim do not reconcile with the quarterly data, and the bear's leverage-stress range is miscomputed. The headline's Synaptics thesis and the $90 target rest on unsupported or incoherent math, and the text leaks internal agent names and chat artifacts, so it is not fit to publish without substantial rework.

The report's core fundamental figures are mostly read correctly, but its technical case and ruling rest on a MACD crossover the computed facts show already happened. An Underweight rating paired with an underived $9.00 target 21% above the price is self-contradictory. Load-bearing misreads (the burn-ratio basis, an invented eight-quarter trend, a fabricated $172M burn rate), a wrong 52-week range, a mis-dated earnings checkpoint and business-model errors make it unfit for publication without substantial rework.

The price-derived technicals match the computed facts, but the fundamentals are built on a misread NT$/US$ unit basis and a debt-to-equity ratio misstated by 100x, both of which feed the digest's bull and bear key points. Exit thresholds and stops conflict across sections, the $520 target has no derivation, and the debate's valuation models and expected-value math are broken, so the note is not publishable as is.

The price-derived technical figures match the computed facts, but the fundamental and valuation work is riddled with load-bearing errors. These include an FCF figure that does not reconcile with OCF minus capex, a phantom 8.7% FCF yield the ruling relies on, and a dividend payout mislabelled as a share of FCF. The deciding 'normalized EPS' tie-breaker is built on cash-flow numbers mislabelled as net income. The final call also rests on contradictory add/trim triggers at $168-170, an underived $165 target, and social posts dated after the trade date treated as fact, so it does not hold up.
